# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto outlines plans to reduce National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual tax cut for average workers. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The party commits to maintaining fiscal rules requiring public sector debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP.

Business support includes maintaining "full expensing" tax policies, keeping corporation tax unchanged, and providing £4.3 billion in business rates support over five years. The manifesto promises continued investment in infrastructure, including £36 billion from HS2 savings redirected to regional transport projects, £8.3 billion for road maintenance, and expanded broadband coverage.

## Immigration and Borders

The manifesto proposes a legally binding annual cap on migration covering work and family visas, with numbers required to fall each year. Parliament would vote annually on cap levels. The Rwanda removal scheme would continue, with regular deportation flights. Asylum processing targets aim for six-month completion, ending hotel accommodation use.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 more doctors. The manifesto includes 250 new or modernised GP surgeries, 50 Community Diagnostic Centres, and expanded pharmacy services. Mental health support would extend to all schools by 2030.

## Housing

A target of 1.6 million new homes includes fast-tracking brownfield development, abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules, and permanent Stamp Duty relief for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000. A new Help to Buy scheme would provide 20% equity loans.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

Defence spending would reach 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in munitions production. Support for Ukraine would continue, alongside strengthened NATO partnerships.

## Energy and Environment

The manifesto commits to net zero by 2050 while guaranteeing no new green levies. Plans include tripling offshore wind capacity, building Small Modular Reactors, and annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds.
